description: A four-bit magnitude comparator: it reads the A inputs and the B inputs as two four-bit numbers and reports which is larger, with cascade inputs so several can be chained.

inputs.text: One bit of the first number: A1 is worth one, A2 two, A3 four and A4 eight.
One bit of the second number: B1 is worth one, B2 two, B3 four and B4 eight.
Read only while the two numbers are equal, when it is copied to the A<B output. Unpatched it counts as low.
Read only while the two numbers are equal, when it is copied to the A=B output. With nothing patched it reads 10V, so a match on this module alone takes the A=B output high.
Read only while the two numbers are equal, when it is copied to the A>B output. Unpatched it counts as low.

outputs.text: 10V while the first number is smaller than the second. While the two are equal this copies the A<B input instead.
10V while the two numbers are equal and the A=B input is high; 0V whenever the numbers differ.
10V while the first number is larger than the second. While the two are equal this copies the A>B input instead.

notes: A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
To compare more than four bits, patch the three outputs of the module carrying the lower bits into the three matching inputs of the module carrying the higher bits.
